title: The River That Boils
description:
Deep in Peru's Amazon, the Shanay-Timpishka river runs hot enough to kill animals that fall in, with readings close to 100°C. The nearest volcano is about 700 km away: rainwater sinks deep underground, heats up and comes back to the surface.

Sources: Andrés Ruzo, The Boiling River (TED Books, 2016); Discover Wildlife, "Shanay-Timpishka boiling river".
Narration is AI-generated text-to-speech and the pictures are AI-generated illustrations.

#shorts #amazon #peru #nature #science

segments.text: This river is hot enough to cook anything that falls in.

segments.text: It's in the Amazon jungle of Peru, and parts of it get close to 100 degrees Celsius.
segments.say: It's in the Amazon jungle of Peru, and parts of it get close to one hundred degrees Celsius.
segments.image: close-up of steaming bubbling hot water rushing over dark rocks in a jungle river, white steam, green leaves, bright daylight

segments.text: Small animals that slip in don't make it out.

segments.text: And the strange part? The nearest volcano is about 700 kilometres away. Rainwater sinks deep underground, heats up, and comes back boiling.
segments.say: And the strange part? The nearest volcano is about seven hundred kilometres away. Rainwater sinks deep underground, heats up, and comes back boiling.
segments.image: cutaway illustration of rainwater seeping down through layers of rock deep underground, glowing hot rock below, water rising back up as steam into a jungle river

segments.text: Would you touch it? Unreal, but true.
